{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement resource cleanup through the existing Spring XD stream lifecycle and message-bus abstraction, rather than adding broker-specific cleanup logic to the core stream model.",
    "Track ownership metadata linking queues, topics, channels, and stream/module identifiers so resources created for a stream can be identified and removed safely.",
    "Make cleanup idempotent and tolerant of already-missing broker resources, while preserving resources explicitly marked as externally managed.",
    "Support stream editing through an update command/API that validates changes and applies them differently for deployed and undeployed streams; deployment-affecting changes trigger the existing redeployment mechanism.",
    "Add deployment-manifest loading from a local file, with validation, clear CLI errors, and equivalent semantics to inline deployment properties.",
    "Represent trace configuration as deployment properties using exact module names and wildcard module patterns, such as module.http.trace and module.*.trace.",
    "Implement trace behavior using Spring Integration wiretaps or equivalent message-channel interception so primary stream behavior is not changed.",
    "Model side channels as optional module-level channel declarations with explicit names and lifecycle ownership, while retaining the existing primary input and output channels.",
    "Provide reference architectures and the taxi-trip work as documented/sample Spring XD artifacts rather than as a new generalized analytics platform.",
    "Use the existing project build, test, CLI, persistence, and messaging conventions wherever possible to minimize compatibility risk."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "All eight user stories are included in the increment, although U5 and U8 are treated primarily as documentation, examples, and demonstrator work.",
    "The existing Spring XD codebase, command-line shell, stream parser, deployment model, persistence layer, and message-bus adapters are available and buildable.",
    "No new message-broker provider, broker protocol, or production-grade distributed garbage collector is required.",
    "Resource ownership metadata can be added to the existing stream or deployment metadata model without a database migration beyond the project's normal schema/versioning mechanism.",
    "Stream editing does not require zero-downtime rolling upgrades; existing undeploy/redeploy behavior may be used where necessary.",
    "Deployment manifests use a documented existing or newly defined text format such as YAML or properties and do not require support for every historical configuration format.",
    "Trace and side-channel functionality is limited to stream/module channels and does not include a separate user interface.",
    "Wildcard matching is limited to the specified module property patterns and uses deterministic precedence rules documented for users.",
    "Reference architectures are limited to raw domain-specific ideas and representative stream definitions, as stated in U5.",
    "The taxi-trip deliverable uses an available or publicly documented sample dataset and produces a reproducible Spring XD stream plus a basic analytical demonstration, not a fully hardened production system.",
    "Effort includes implementation, focused code review, automated tests, documentation, and local integration validation, but excludes project-management overhead, major framework upgrades, and external stakeholder workshops.",
    "The estimates represent one developer's work-hours and are most-likely estimates rather than optimistic or pessimistic bounds."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Repository and requirement analysis",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing Spring XD stream lifecycle, deployment commands, persistence model, message-bus adapters, module channels, test conventions, and relevant documentation; refine acceptance criteria for all user stories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Cross-cutting design and implementation planning",
      "activity_description": "Define resource ownership, cleanup semantics, stream update behavior, manifest structure, trace matching and precedence, side-channel representation, compatibility behavior, and test strategy.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Coupled message-bus resource cleanup",
      "activity_description": "Implement U1 cleanup of queues/topics and related channels owned by a stream when the stream is destroyed, including lifecycle hooks, ownership tracking, idempotent deletion, error handling, and CLI/API integration.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Stale resource discovery and cleanup",
      "activity_description": "Implement U2 detection and cleanup of stale queues/topics associated with destroyed or incomplete streams, including safe filtering, missing-resource handling, and an invocable cleanup operation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 36
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Stream editing for deployed and undeployed streams",
      "activity_description": "Implement U3 command/API support for changing stream definitions or deployment properties, validation, persistence updates, state-specific behavior, and redeployment or synchronization of affected resources.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Deployment manifest file support",
      "activity_description": "Implement U4 loading deployment properties from a file, parsing and validation, command-line integration, error reporting, precedence rules, and documentation/examples.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Optional module trace configuration",
      "activity_description": "Implement U6 trace deployment properties for exact module names and wildcard patterns, resolve matching modules, configure Spring Integration wiretaps or equivalent interceptors, and handle invalid or conflicting configuration.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Module side-channel support",
      "activity_description": "Implement U7 declarations and lifecycle management for arbitrary optional side channels within a module flow, including channel creation, wiring, naming, persistence, deployment, undeployment, and cleanup integration.",
      "most_likely_effort": 64
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature integration and compatibility work",
      "activity_description": "Integrate cleanup, editing, manifests, tracing, and side channels across stream parsing, deployment, module lifecycle, persistence, and message-bus adapters; resolve backward-compatibility issues.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Automated unit and integration testing",
      "activity_description": "Add tests for lifecycle cleanup, stale-resource handling, stream edits, manifest parsing, trace exact and wildcard matching, side-channel wiring, broker interactions, failure recovery, and regression coverage.",
      "most_likely_effort": 72
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Spring XD reference architectures",
      "activity_description": "Deliver U5 raw domain-specific reference architecture ideas, representative stream definitions, deployment manifests, explanatory notes, and instructions for using them to build proof-of-concept applications.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "Taxi-trip event-stream demonstrator",
      "activity_description": "Deliver U8 a reproducible taxi-trip data ingestion and processing stream, sample data preparation, real-time or near-real-time analytical flow, result interpretation, and a short evaluation of event-based processing.",
      "most_likely_effort": 64
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A13",
      "activity_name": "User and developer documentation",
      "activity_description": "Document new commands, APIs, manifest syntax, cleanup behavior, trace and side-channel properties, examples, operational cautions, reference architectures, and the taxi-trip demonstrator.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A14",
      "activity_name": "Final validation and release preparation",
      "activity_description": "Run the full build and regression suite, perform manual CLI and broker-backed smoke tests, review configuration defaults and upgrade behavior, fix release-blocking defects, and prepare release notes.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 576
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement resource cleanup through the existing Spring XD stream lifecycle and message-bus abstraction, rather than adding broker-specific cleanup logic to the core stream model.
Track ownership metadata linking queues, topics, channels, and stream/module identifiers so resources created for a stream can be identified and removed safely.
Make cleanup idempotent and tolerant of already-missing broker resources, while preserving resources explicitly marked as externally managed.

Support stream editing through an update command/API that validates changes and applies them differently for deployed and undeployed streams; deployment-affecting changes trigger the existing redeployment mechanism.
Add deployment-manifest loading from a local file, with validation, clear CLI errors, and equivalent semantics to inline deployment properties.
Represent trace configuration as deployment properties using exact module names and wildcard module patterns, such as module.http.trace and module.*.trace.
Implement trace behavior using Spring Integration wiretaps or equivalent message-channel interception so primary stream behavior is not changed.
Model side channels as optional module-level channel declarations with explicit names and lifecycle ownership, while retaining the existing primary input and output channels.
Provide reference architectures and the taxi-trip work as documented/sample Spring XD artifacts rather than as a new generalized analytics platform.
Use the existing project build, test, CLI, persistence, and messaging conventions wherever possible to minimize compatibility risk.
assumptions: All eight user stories are included in the increment, although U5 and U8 are treated primarily as documentation, examples, and demonstrator work.
The existing Spring XD codebase, command-line shell, stream parser, deployment model, persistence layer, and message-bus adapters are available and buildable.
No new message-broker provider, broker protocol, or production-grade distributed garbage collector is required.
Resource ownership metadata can be added to the existing stream or deployment metadata model without a database migration beyond the project's normal schema/versioning mechanism.
Stream editing does not require zero-downtime rolling upgrades; existing undeploy/redeploy behavior may be used where necessary.
Deployment manifests use a documented existing or newly defined text format such as YAML or properties and do not require support for every historical configuration format.
Trace and side-channel functionality is limited to stream/module channels and does not include a separate user interface.
Wildcard matching is limited to the specified module property patterns and uses deterministic precedence rules documented for users.
Reference architectures are limited to raw domain-specific ideas and representative stream definitions, as stated in U5.

The taxi-trip deliverable uses an available or publicly documented sample dataset and produces a reproducible Spring XD stream plus a basic analytical demonstration, not a fully hardened production system.

Effort includes implementation, focused code review, automated tests, documentation, and local integration validation, but excludes project-management overhead, major framework upgrades, and external stakeholder workshops.
The estimates represent one developer's work-hours and are most-likely estimates rather than optimistic or pessimistic bounds.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing Spring XD stream lifecycle, deployment commands, persistence model, message-bus adapters, module channels, test conventions, and relevant documentation; refine acceptance criteria for all user stories.
Define resource ownership, cleanup semantics, stream update behavior, manifest structure, trace matching and precedence, side-channel representation, compatibility behavior, and test strategy.

Implement U1 cleanup of queues/topics and related channels owned by a stream when the stream is destroyed, including lifecycle hooks, ownership tracking, idempotent deletion, error handling, and CLI/API integration.
Implement U2 detection and cleanup of stale queues/topics associated with destroyed or incomplete streams, including safe filtering, missing-resource handling, and an invocable cleanup operation.

activities.activity_name: Stream editing for deployed and undeployed streams
activities.activity_description: Implement U3 command/API support for changing stream definitions or deployment properties, validation, persistence updates, state-specific behavior, and redeployment or synchronization of affected resources.
Implement U4 loading deployment properties from a file, parsing and validation, command-line integration, error reporting, precedence rules, and documentation/examples.

Implement U6 trace deployment properties for exact module names and wildcard patterns, resolve matching modules, configure Spring Integration wiretaps or equivalent interceptors, and handle invalid or conflicting configuration.

Implement U7 declarations and lifecycle management for arbitrary optional side channels within a module flow, including channel creation, wiring, naming, persistence, deployment, undeployment, and cleanup integration.
Integrate cleanup, editing, manifests, tracing, and side channels across stream parsing, deployment, module lifecycle, persistence, and message-bus adapters; resolve backward-compatibility issues.

Add tests for lifecycle cleanup, stale-resource handling, stream edits, manifest parsing, trace exact and wildcard matching, side-channel wiring, broker interactions, failure recovery, and regression coverage.

Deliver U5 raw domain-specific reference architecture ideas, representative stream definitions, deployment manifests, explanatory notes, and instructions for using them to build proof-of-concept applications.

Deliver U8 a reproducible taxi-trip data ingestion and processing stream, sample data preparation, real-time or near-real-time analytical flow, result interpretation, and a short evaluation of event-based processing.
Document new commands, APIs, manifest syntax, cleanup behavior, trace and side-channel properties, examples, operational cautions, reference architectures, and the taxi-trip demonstrator.
Run the full build and regression suite, perform manual CLI and broker-backed smoke tests, review configuration defaults and upgrade behavior, fix release-blocking defects, and prepare release notes.
